doc.title: Hentoff Nat — Smithsonian Jazz Oral History

title: Desert-island records
summary: He would take The Sound of Jazz, Kansas City Six, Basie, Ellington's Fargo date and Coltrane.

story.theme_name: In the studio: making records, then and now
story.community_name: Writing, arranging and composing: how the music gets made

blocks.x: If you were to have a desert-island list – if the building were burning, however you want to phrase it – what records – what albums would you like to have with you.

In view of advancing technology, of which I’m usually very ignorant, I would take a high-definition television set and bring with me The Sound of Jazz. Otherwise, the usual choices: Kansas City Six or anything by Lester [Young], Basie, Ellington – especially Fargo – the Fargo, North Dakota, date – some of Coltrane. All kinds of things. I couldn’t – if I had to limit myself, I would consider that a violation of the Eighth Amendment, cruel and unusual punishment. There’s so much.
